title: Identifying the Physics Behind an Electric Motor
provider: Department of Power Electronics and Electrical Drives (LEA), Paderborn University; released via Kaggle.

record_hash.representation: parsed Kaggle JSON serialized by json.dumps with default Python settings

keys: Identifying the Physics Behind an Electric Motor

separation: The related LEA current transition, stationary torque grid, and thermal drive-cycle releases involve distinct acquisitions and lack a common test identifier. Do not join individual files across releases.
creator: Kaggle release by Hanke, with Sören Hanke, Oliver Wallscheid and Joachim Böcker named on Parts I and II of the dataset description.
rights: Kaggle displays “Data files © Original Authors”. No express redistribution license for the raw measurements was verified. Only independently computed summary statistics, digests and a reader are shared; source measurements and PDFs remain at source.
query_log: Followed the “Currents and motor speed per switching state” cross-link from Electric Motor Temperature to the distinct Hanke public release; verified v4 by Kaggle API and the fixed individual file.

Followed the release links to both arXiv full texts. Part I defines elementary vectors and ordering; Part II supplies the operating envelope and deliberate random replacements. Compared version/slug, normalized title and both arXiv IDs with all project evidence text and the early index.

papers.title: Data Set Description: Identifying the Physics Behind an Electric Motor – Data-Driven Learning of the Electrical Behavior (Part I)
papers.locator: Section III and Table II. Each row gives both axes of current at k and k+1, applied elementary vector and previous vector. The authors explicitly state that successive file rows do not constitute a time series.

papers.title: Data Set Description: Identifying the Physics Behind an Electric Motor – Data-Driven Learning of the Electrical Behavior (Part II)
papers.locator: Tables III–IV and Fig. 4. 57 kW traction IPMSM bench; fixed 1000 rpm, 300 V, approximately 55 °C, controller period 50 μs. Maximum allowed dq current vector length 240 A. To cover the current plane, 478 different setpoints and deliberate random substitutions of some MPC-selected elementary vectors were used.

measurement: For each released row, evaluate hypot(id_k,iq_k) and hypot(id_k1,iq_k1) against the paper’s 240 A dq operating range. Classify strict exceeds. Group by previous and applied switch-vector index. A row crossing a current threshold reports a physical current measurement after the applied action; it does not establish clipping of the requested command.
limits: No pre-limiter request, output limiter flag, thermal derating flag, phase-by-phase actuator fault flag, or per-row indicator of which actions were randomly substituted. The data do not identify the dynamics of an untouched closed-loop policy or the duration of an over-current episode.

The article’s 240 A is a specified operating range, not the current measurement chain’s ADC rail. Report the measured dq norm before and after each vector. Adjacent file rows cannot be used to reconstruct dwell times: not a single adjacent pair has both preceding end currents exactly equal to the following start currents. Exact equality was checked on both published numerical coordinates without rounding.

The 49 transitions cover 7 discrete vector indices, with unequal cell counts. Transition-conditioned statistics reflect both selected operating points and applied input; no randomized-group causal comparison is claimed.
reproduce: Python >=3.11 with numpy and pandas. OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python derive_switch_currents.py SOURCE_V4_FILE_ZIP OUT.
